about: Pigment library for the studio's media, from measured data. Every number has a source in `sources`; derived values (sRGB, engine K/S) are computed by tools from the measurements with CIE 1931 2-degree observer, D65, 400-700 nm at 10 nm. 'engine.over_white/over_black' are the inputs of studio/v8/media/base.py pigment(); they are sRGB-encoded 0..1 like the engine's hx() colours. Built 2026-11-25 (see docs/media-data.md).

revigo.cite: M. Geldof, A. Proano Gaibor, F. Ligterink, E. Hendriks, E. Kirchner, 'Reconstructing Van Gogh's palette to determine the optical characteristics of his paints', Heritage Science 6:17 (2018)
revigo.method: hand-ground oil paints (19th-c. recipes and Kremer pigments), drawn down 'relatively uniform layer of 100 um thickness' on a BYK-Gardner black-and-white chart, Konica Minolta CM-2600d d/8 SCI, 400-700 nm / 10 nm. Suffixes: _b black chart, _ob paint over black, _ow paint over white, _w white chart. K and S per wavelength fitted here by two-constant Kubelka-Munk (x = 1 film) after removing a Saunderson correction with the paper's k1 = 0.04, k2 = 0.49.
revigo.status: measured; K/S fit computed for this file (the repo's own K/S notebook is empty)

fors.cite: A. Cosentino, 'FORS spectral database of historical pigments in different binders', e-conservation Journal 2 (2014) 57-68
fors.data: https://chsopensource.org/new-free-pigments-fors-spectroscopy-database (zip of CSV: gum arabic, egg tempera, linseed oil, fresco, powder; 360-1000 nm)
fors.method: 54 historical pigments (Pigments Checker swatches) measured with a fibre-optic reflectance spectrometer and integrating sphere. The CSV scale is relative (whites read 100-135%, carbon blacks ~10%); here each binder set is normalised per wavelength so lamp black = 0.03 and titanium white = 0.90 (assumed values), so absolute values are approximate. Use for hue and for ranking pigments by value within a binder; the Revigo oil data and handprint values are the calibrated ones.
fors.status: measured spectra; absolute scale not verified; licence not stated (data offered for free download)

handprint.cite: B. MacEvoy, handprint.com 'guide to watercolor pigments' (rev. 2015), ratings of 750+ commercial watercolour paints
handprint.method: per paint: Tr transparency 0 (very opaque)-4, St staining 0-4, VR value range (paper value minus masstone value, 100-step scale), Gr granulation 0 (liquid)-4, Bl blossom 0-4, Df diffusion wet-in-wet 0 (inert)-4, HA CIELAB hue angle (GretagMacbeth spectrophotometer). Medians over the brands tested, per Colour Index name. CIECAM J,a,b masstone and drying shift parsed from the notes where given.
handprint.status: one experienced tester's standardised swatch tests: ratings are ordinal judgements, colour values are instrument measurements; not peer reviewed

lbnl.cite: R. Levinson, P. Berdahl, H. Akbari, 'Solar spectral optical properties of pigments, Part I: model for deriving scattering and absorption coefficients from transmittance and reflectance measurements' and 'Part II: survey of common colorants', Solar Energy Materials & Solar Cells 89 (2005) 319-349, 351-389; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Pigment Database
lbnl.method: artists' acrylic paints (Liquitex) drawn down as thin films (about 15-30 um) and measured over a void (R and T), an opaque white and an opaque black, 300-2500 nm; K and S (mm^-1) computed per film by LBNL. Masstones and 1:4 and 1:9 tints (volume) with titanium white W03. The numeric datafiles are encrypted for the project's partners; the values here were read from the public vector charts by tools/pigments/lbnl_charts.py (exact to the plotted precision). Earth K and S here: masstone-tint fit (Duncan, volume fractions) on each film's R_inf; scaled to the Revigo film unit (lbnl_scale).
lbnl.status: measured, acrylic binder (refractive index ~1.49, close to linseed oil's ~1.48), used as oil proxies; yellow and red iron oxide are synthetic proxies for yellow and red ochre; burnt umber and green earth are approximations (FORS masstone + borrowed scattering); licence not stated (a US national laboratory's public web pages)

curtis1997.cite: C. J. Curtis et al., 'Computer-Generated Watercolor', SIGGRAPH 1997, Fig. 5
curtis1997.status: NOT measured: K and S were derived from colours the authors chose by eye over white and black; density, staining power and granularity are the authors' simulation settings. Kept as the graphics baseline the studio's watercolour follows.

lbnl_scale.note: LBNL K, S (per mm) x this factor = per Revigo film. Within LBNL (earth + titanium white) mixing is measured; between an LBNL paint and a Revigo paint the relative strength is uncertain by about the spread factor.

fors_calibration.method: FORS linseed oil, normalised per wavelength (lamp black 0.03, titanium white 0.90), as for masstone_by_binder
fors_calibration.note_error: FORS-derived masstone vs LBNL-measured masstone of the same pigment name (different samples and binders): the expected error of the two approximations
fors_calibration.note_proxy: FORS natural ochre vs the LBNL synthetic iron oxide used for it
